item.title: Trump’s Border Czar Announces 700 Immigration Officers To Immediately Leave Minnesota
item.description: By STEVE KARNOWSKI Associated Press MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — The Trump administration is reducing the number of immigration enforcement officers in Minnesota after state and local officials agreed to cooperate by turning over arrested immigrants, border czar Tom Homan said Wednesday. item.title: Olympic Transgender Policy
item.description: The Olympics, which start this week, is expected to be the last one held under the current rules that allow transgender athletes to compete against women. Congressman Chip Roy of Texas hopes that gets changed by the IOC. He spoke this week during the markup of what has been dubbed the “Protection of Women in Olympic and Amateur Sports Act.” It would add a new rule, requiring amateur sports organizations to ban trans girls in order to be eligible for certification.

item.title: Self Driving Cars
item.description: Waymo’s Chief Safety Officer is addressing the investigation into reports that their self-driving cars are going around stopped school buses in Austin, endangering kids. Mauricio Peña says they’re working with the School District to figure out what is happening. There have been at least 19 incidents of Waymo’s cars driving past stopped school buses around the state capitol.

item.title: Protest Fight Arrest
item.description: A Texas man who was caught on camera fighting with student protesters has been arrested. Chad Watts is charged with assault. The incident erupted in the Austin suburb of Buda this week, as hundreds of high schoolers left class to protest ICE raids. Police say that Watts started arguing with a girl, left his truck and attacked her. The 45-year-old was then swarmed by students before speeding away.

item.title: School District Investigation
item.description: Governor Greg Abbott is ordering the Texas Education Commissioner to investigate student protests over ICE raids. He says in a statement that he is also looking into stripping the funding of schools that abandon their duty to teach our kids the curriculum required by law.

item.title: Social Studies Curriculum
item.description: The Texas State Board of Education has crafted a wish list of historical topics that will guide social studies classes. Democrats pushed for young children to learn about slavery, which was opposed by Republican Julie Pickren. She says Africans were not the only slaves, but that’s all kids would learn about. The overhaul started last year. Final decisions are due this summer. The new curriculum will start in the year 2030.

item.title: AG Sues Bexar
item.description: AG Ken Paxton is suing Bexar County for using taxpayer dollars to defend illegal immigrants in court. It’s something that San Antonio Republicans have been trying to stop. Kris Coons, who heads the Bexar County Republican Party, says that taxpayer dollars should be spent on basic services, like street repairs and public safety. The AG agrees. He said that funding legal services for non-citizens offers “no public benefit” and serves “private radical interests.”

item.title: Still No Suspect In The Disappearance Of ‘Today’ Host Savannah Guthrie’s Mother
item.description: By JACQUES BILLEAUD, SEJAL GOVINDARAO and MIKE BALSAMO Associated Pressearch for “Today” show host Savannah Guthrie’s mother still had no suspect or person of interest Wednesday, authorities said, four days after she disappeared with signs of forced entry at her home in southern Arizona. Investigators believe Nancy Guthrie was taken against her will over the weekend and Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos has said they don’t have credible information indicating Guthrie’s disappearance was targeted.
